liam: Quick sync: picking internal surface for routing policy RPCs. Proto/gRPC vs JSON/REST? Key constraints: quotas, console UX, rollout signals, and browser compatibility.
jen: Proto wins for strong contracts and easier quota attribution. JSON wins for discoverability and cURL examples.
arik: Can we do JSON at edge -> gRPC internal? concern: added latency + ops complexity, especially for streaming.
dan: For routing policies typed route_keys are gold. Avoids brittle proxy parsers.
sasha: Browser teams still hit issues with gRPC-web setup last quarter. That's not hypothetical.
liam: Telemetry: with proto we can add explicit route tags in the envelope for exact per-route metrics. With JSON we either parse or infer.
arik: Rollout UX: canarying model variants per route needs stable canonical keys. Proto helps.
jen: Console friendly samples matter for PLG. JSON snippets are easier for docs and quickstarts.
dan: Operational compromise: translator at the edge that validates JSON, emits signed X-Route-Claim header, then forwards internal gRPC. Pros: typed backends. Cons: translator is extra state and CPU.
liam: Quotas: enforce at edge (fast failure) or backend (authoritative)? Edge early enforcement duplicates logic; backend needs reliable route info.
dan: Header signing idea: edge validates + signs X-Route-Claim: "tenant:acct_123;route:text-complete;nonce:...". Backend verifies signature and enforces quota.
sasha: Signing is fine but add key rotation, audit, and Console visibility. I want the header visible in request inspector.
liam: Example mapping:
```http
POST /v1/generate
Accept: application/json
X-Tenant: acct_123
Body: {"route":"text-complete","input":"foo"}
# Edge -> translate -> internal gRPC: GenerateRequest{ tenant_id: "acct_123", route_key: "text-complete", prompt: "foo" }
```
jen: Streaming differences: bridging chunked JSON and gRPC streaming requires a translator that can shuttle frames without amplifying latency.
arik: Failure modes: translator outage -> fallback to JSON passthrough or require direct gRPC clients. Need graceful degrade plan.
liam: Proposal: 3-month dual-mode POC: JSON fronting + internal proto. Build a lightweight shim that emits signed X-Route-Claim and trace id. Canary on small tenant slice.
jen: I'll do cost/latency estimate for the translator (ETA Wed).
sasha: I'll prototype Console inspector changes and a toggle for viewing proto fields (ETA Mon).
arik: I'll spin up POC repo & latency bench (ETA Fri).
dan: I'll draft header signing + rotation doc (ETA next Tue).
liam: React :thumbsup: if you agree to dual-mode POC.
